title: DS-GL: Advancing Graph Learning via Harnessing Nature's Power within Scalable Dynamical Systems
problem: Graph learning tasks require tremendous computational power due to inherent complexity and irregularity. CMOS-compatible Ising machines face two critical limitations: they are binary (ill-suited for real-valued problems) and have expensive all-to-all coupling networks that create severe scalability concerns.
motivation: Real-world applications increasingly rely on non-Euclidean graph data, requiring efficient hardware acceleration for graph learning tasks.
method: DS-GL augments the Ising machine architecture by modifying the Hamiltonian's self-reaction term from linear to quadratic, enabling processing of continuous real-valued data while maintaining physical interpretability. The framework decomposes the dense Ising machine into a mesh-based multi-PE dynamical system supporting distributed spatial-temporal co-annealing through sparse interconnects. By exploiting inherent sparsity and community structures in real-world graphs, complex graph learning tasks are mapped onto the scalable system while preserving accuracy.
key_novelty: First framework transforming graph learning into natural annealing processes within CMOS-based dynamical systems, handling real-valued data and scaling through mesh-based decomposition.
contributions: Augmented Ising machine with quadratic Hamiltonian modification for continuous real-valued data processing
Mesh-based multi-PE decomposition enabling scalable distributed spatial-temporal co-annealing
First mapping of complex graph learning tasks onto hardware dynamical systems
Demonstration of 10³ to 10⁵× speedups with 2 orders of magnitude lower power than GPU-based GNNs

metrics.speedup: 10^3× to 10^5× over Graph Neural Networks on GPU
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2 orders of magnitude lower power than GPU

primary_theme: Hardware-accelerated graph learning via CMOS dynamical systems
